reasoning: The product 'aluminium window frames' directly matches tariff line 76101000 ('Doors, windows and their frames and thresholds for doors (aluminium)').
Tariff line 76101000 is preferential under the India-UAE CEPA with a 2026 CEPA rate of 0%.
The effective MFN rate is 10% and the preferential CEPA rate is 0%.
Under PSR-IN-R118, the rule is CTSH + VA 45%; the product qualifies based on a CTSH pass for all 3 non-originating inputs and a 49.0% value addition on an FOB basis.
Duty savings are estimated at 10000.00 AED based on the 100000.00 AED shipment value and a 10 percentage point duty difference.
Because origin qualifies, the procedural steps detail factory registration, certificate application, fee payment, export requirements, and importer actions.
Caveats highlight CIF valuation by Indian customs, BCD scope, self-declaration reliance, interpretation of rule operators, free-zone registration restrictions, and certificate issuer details.

classification.description: Doors, windows and their frames and thresholds for doors (aluminium)

origin_result.basis: Declared final manufacture took place in the UAE, and manufacturing goes beyond minimal operations. All 3 non-originating inputs are classified outside subheading 761010 (CTSH pass). Qualifying value addition is 49.0% by build-down against a 45% threshold on an FOB price basis, with non-originating inputs accounting for 51% of the price across 6 total inputs.

procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism requires the factory to be registered through its Factory Registration service prior to applying for a certificate, which requires a factory located outside a free zone, a MoIAT industrial licence, and a MoIAT letter confirming 40% domestic value added (taking about 3 working days).
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The Ministry of Foreign Trade provides the Certificate of Origin for India e-service where applicants submit proof of factory registration and the commercial invoice, with processing taking about one working day.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade charges a certificate fee of AED 50 for an invoice value up to AED 100000.

The competent authority issues the certificate of origin prior to, at, or within 5 working days of exportation, bearing an authorised signature and official seal, valid for 12 months for a single import.
The exporter must ensure the goods are consigned directly from the UAE to India without undergoing operations in third countries other than unloading, reloading, or storage under customs supervision.
The exporter must keep origin records, including cost breakdowns, for at least 5 years starting from the end of the year of the certificate's issue.

The Indian importer must claim the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry, maintain supporting origin information for at least 5 years under CAROTAR 2020, and answer any customs origin verification inquiries within 10 working days.

caveats.note: No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
Duty is estimated on the shipment value given, but India charges customs duty on the assessable CIF value at import, so actual amounts will differ.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS), and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
Verification of operations and final manufacture relies on the exporter's own declaration.
'+' in a rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India.
